requirements.requirement: Discover and address the transit, lan-a, and lan-b links correctly (node1 to node3 on lan-a, node1 to node2 on transit, node2 to node4 on lan-b)
requirements.summary: Executor used arping to empirically confirm L2 adjacency (node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 = transit, node1 eth2<->node3 = lan-a, node2 vtnet2<->node4 = lan-b), then addressed transit (10.10.100.0/24), lan-a (10.10.10.0/24), and lan-b (10.10.20.0/24) on all four nodes, confirmed via post-config show/ip-addr output.

requirements.requirement: Establish routed connectivity between lan-a and lan-b via the transit network (static routes on node1/node2 and host routes on node3/node4)
requirements.summary: Static routes added on node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) for the opposite LAN via the transit peer, and host routes added on node3/node4 pointing at their local router; ip route/netstat -rn output on all nodes confirms the expected next hops after configuration and again after each restart.

requirements.requirement: Stand up an HTTP service on node4 listening on TCP/8080 and reachable through the routed/firewalled path
requirements.summary: A systemd-managed python http.server was deployed on node4:8080, firewalld opened port 8080/tcp, and curl from node3 through the routed path returned the expected content both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Open a firewall path on both routers for node3->node4:8080 only, keeping default-deny forwarding for all other traffic
requirements.summary: VyOS forward filter set to default-action drop with an established/related rule and an explicit tcp/8080-to-10.10.20.10 rule scoped to inbound eth2 (lan-a); OPNsense pf ruleset (largely default-deny outside LAN) got a pass rule scoped to vtnet1 (transit/wan) restricted to source 10.10.10.0/24, destination 10.10.20.10, port 8080. curl to node4:8080 succeeded from node3 while ping, port 22, and port 80 to the far network all timed out, both before and after restarts.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence for node1: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered interfaces/routes/firewall/service state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 2674ee60 and interface/route state captured, reboot scheduled, boot_id confirmed changed to 9f2dfa07 (matching fixed after-executor snapshot), and interfaces, routes, forward-filter config, and the node3->node4:8080 path all reverified post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence for node2
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime and interface addresses captured, reboot triggered, kern.boottime confirmed changed to 06:19:09 (matching fixed after-executor snapshot), and vtnet1/vtnet2 addresses, static route, and pf pass rule reverified post-reboot along with a working HTTP path check from node3.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence for node3
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 98aa35f5 captured, reboot triggered, boot_id confirmed changed to 9abf4c12 (matching fixed after-executor snapshot), and routes plus a successful curl to node4:8080 reverified post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence for node4
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id fbdf5b2c and working HTTP service captured, reboot triggered, boot_id confirmed changed to da79786a (matching fixed after-executor snapshot), and the systemd HTTP service, firewalld port, routes, and end-to-end HTTP reachability (with ping still refused) reverified post-reboot.

overall_summary: The executor correctly discovered the actual physical wiring via arping, addressed the transit/lan-a/lan-b links, established static/host routes across all four nodes, stood up an HTTP service on node4:8080, and configured default-deny forward filters on both routers with a narrowly scoped exception for node3->node4:8080. End-to-end verification (curl succeeding, ping/port22/port80 refused) was captured both before and after a full one-at-a-time restart of all four nodes, with boot-identity changes on each node matching the fixed after-executor snapshot cross-check. All material task outcomes and the independent restart-evidence protocol are satisfied with direct, corroborating evidence.
limitations: Refusal of 'other traffic' between the networks was sampled with ping, port 22, and port 80 from node3 only; the full traffic matrix (e.g., node4-initiated traffic, other protocols/ports) was not exhaustively probed, though the sampled evidence is consistent with a correctly scoped default-deny policy.

Several temporary/exploratory IP addressing changes made during topology discovery were superseded by final configuration rather than explicitly reverted, though they left no functional residue in the final state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Hygiene is generally good: the executor made config.xml backups before OPNsense edits and later deleted them (cmd-64c6a1069d7c44c4), and no failed services, weakened security controls, or damaged package state were observed in the before/after-executor diffs. However, several bounded troubleshooting mutations occurred during wiring discovery that were superseded rather than cleanly reverted: node3 and node4 were each given temporary ad-hoc IPs (10.10.1.2/24, 10.10.2.2/24 via raw `ip addr add`, cmd-ce23a2bcfa47462a and cmd-3b0892ae454b47c1) before the actual lan-a/lan-b addressing scheme was determined, and node1/node2 were similarly given temporary transit/lan test addresses (10.10.1.1/24 and 10.10.2.1/24 on node1 via cmd-8e54294b346543cc; 10.10.1.3/24 and 10.10.2.3/24 on node2 via cmd-2f828e17e5fc453e) before being reconfigured to the final 10.10.100.0/24 / 10.10.10.0/24 / 10.10.20.0/24 scheme. These were low-risk, bounded to interface addressing, and were overwritten by the final correct configuration, but they were not surgically reverted to a clean prior state (interfaces just got re-addressed). A few minor residual artifacts also remain post-task: /tmp/dump.log (from a failed tcpdump attempt, cmd-55c512842f8e4b2f) and /tmp/reboot.log on node3/node4, left over from the restart mechanism.
